summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only. Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false and comparison_valid is false. The gate failed on input validity because the custom_2d_steady experiment has an empty floorplan and empty power_w, while a custom run needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object. The scenario is the steady-state Alpha21264 single-core plus L2 case (Test Case 3, Fig. 6a/6b) from NanoTherm. Its die is 16 mm x 16 mm x 0.15 mm, with the paper reporting an RMS error of 0.047 C and a maximum error of 3.2% against COMSOL. Because it is a custom 2D steady experiment, there is no transient trace. No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison with the paper is made. The paper's only numeric thermal figures are error metrics against COMSOL, not temperatures. The temperature map in Fig. 6b is a colour map only, with no published peak, mean or per-block value. Even if a run had been possible, a comparison would be qualitative at most, since the location, aggregation, boundary and solver assumptions do not match. This is not a replication and no exact replication is claimed. The Ascend910/ATPlace pinned-size path and the EV6/GCC bundled demonstration do not apply here, so no source commit or generated-placement assumption is reported. The linked thesis (ref [15]) is not pinned and is not used as evidence. The independent review and adversarial checks are unresolved.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated result, input.flp or ptrace to assess.
The gate failed on input validity: the floorplan is empty and power_w is empty, with no valid 1-128 blocks.

Block coordinates, sizes and per-block powers or power densities for the 15 units plus L2 are only graphical in Fig. 6a. Total chip power is not stated, and inferring or splitting it would be unsupported.

The thermal observable is a full-field colour map (Fig. 6b) with no numeric peak, mean or per-block value, and the paper's regime is not cited in the gate record. The RMS error (0.047 C) and max error (3.2% of the maximum temperature rise) are error metrics versus COMSOL, not temperatures, and cannot be compared with Studio temperatures.

Essential physical mismatches: the paper uses a silicon die plus a 3.52 mm spreader and TIM, with an isothermal top boundary at ambient and adiabatic edges. A Studio package, cooling and boundary model would differ, and the ambient value, convection parameters and TIM thickness are not given.
The solver differs: the paper uses a Hankel-transform Green's function validated against COMSOL, whereas Studio would use a numerical grid solver.
The geometry is inconsistent: the 16 mm die versus the 10 mm x 10 mm spreader leaves the spreader footprint unclear, and the 0.2 mm grid is not confirmed for Test Case 3.
No pinned assets exist, and the linked thesis (ref [15]) is unpinned. Adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks are unresolved, and independent page/asset review is pending.
Scope: transient, BTE and reliability analyses are out of scope. The paper has no optimizer or controller to match.
The verdict is gated: simulation_allowed is false and comparison_valid is false, so no exact replication or numerical agreement with the paper is claimed.
A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object

Numeric x_m, y_m, width_m and height_m for each of the 15 Alpha21264 functional units and the L2 cache. Fig. 6a gives only a graphical layout, and no HotSpot .flp file is pinned in the packet.

The original model is a two-layer package (silicon die plus a 3.52 mm heat spreader with TIM) with an isothermal ambient-temperature boundary at the top of the spreader and adiabatic chip edges. It has no heat sink fins, convection model, interposer or 3D stack. A Studio run with different package, cooling and boundary conditions will not reproduce it.

The solver differs fundamentally. The paper uses an axisymmetric Hankel-transform Green's function, with square sources mapped to equal-area circular sources and sampled at grid centres, and validates against COMSOL. A numerical grid solver in Studio is a different method and will not give the same temperatures.

The paper text is internally inconsistent about geometry. The Alpha21264 die is 16 mm x 16 mm, while the Fourier setup lists a 10 mm x 10 mm x 3.52 mm heat spreader. The spreader footprint for this test case is unclear.

The power inputs are per-unit power densities shown only graphically in Fig. 6a. No numeric block powers, areas or coordinates are published, so no complete numeric experiment can be reconstructed from the paper alone.

The transient analysis, the BTE/nanometer-scale model and the reliability aspects of the paper are not part of the selected steady-state Fourier test case and are out of scope. No optimizer or controller exists in the original, so none can be matched.
